name: Syndrel
description: Syndrel is a synthetic oxytocin-vasopressin complex with SNT-pathway amplification that dramatically enhances social bonding, trust formation, and interpersonal attachment between users who take it in proximity to one another. The bond formed under Syndrel feels — and to neurological testing, reads — as genuine. Lazarus markets three distinct product lines: Syndrel Professional (corporate team-building and negotiation), Syndrel Intimate (couples and family counseling), and Syndrel Connect (social anxiety therapeutic). All three are the same formula at the same dose.
effects: intense feelings of trust and warmth toward people present during the drug window
accelerated interpersonal bonding and attachment formation
sense of shared purpose and group identity
side_effects: manufactured bonds can persist beyond the drug window — users may feel genuinely attached to people they barely know
trust formed under Syndrel does not reflect actual trustworthiness of the other party — exploitation risk is significant
jealousy and separation distress if bonded parties are separated post-dose
used without consent, it constitutes chemical coercion — this occurs frequently
some users experience bond dissolution grief when the drug clears, similar to a sudden breakup
duration: 8–12 hours; residual attachment effects can persist for weeks
cultural_context: Syndrel is simultaneously one of the most used and most debated drugs in GLMZ. Corporate team-building retreats in Tier 3-4 routinely incorporate Syndrel under clinical euphemisms like 'cohesion facilitation.' Several Tier 4-5 mergers have been negotiated by both parties under disclosed Syndrel use, with the argument that the drug simply accelerates genuine goodwill. Ethicists and several courts have drawn a hard line at non-disclosed use — which is technically illegal and practically common. In relationships, it's used by couples seeking to rebuild connection, but the question of whether a Syndrel-rebuilt bond is a real bond haunts its users. On the Shelf, it's sold in counterfeit patch form with inconsistent dosing, and has been implicated in multiple cult-formation incidents.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 woman realizes her entire social circle — her closest friendships, her current relationship, her workplace loyalties — were seeded at a company retreat three years ago where Syndrel was in the catered drinks. She doesn't know who she actually loves.

A Shelf community organizer has been using Syndrel to build genuine solidarity in a neighborhood fractured by gang violence. It's working. A corponation that wants the neighborhood destabilized wants to know how to stop him.

A Tier 4 divorce lawyer has built her entire practice on representing clients in 'Syndrel marriages' — relationships that felt real but were chemically accelerated. She's just discovered her own marriage began at a Syndrel event.
